artifacts.plan:
Visitors should quickly understand why they might choose Refine: it coordinates supported coding agents across existing repositories and machines, provides a durable delivery workflow, and keeps code and history under their control. Present those benefits through a compact capability matrix with recognizable symbols and short labels, supported by expandable explanations.

1. [ ] Task #1 - Define concrete comparison criteria.
   Refactor the content in src/surfaces/website/index.html around approximately six capabilities: MIT open source; local repository/runtime ownership; supported installed coding agents; configurable delivery and review steps; coordination across machines; and isolated work with retained recovery evidence. Keep the existing comparison set: Direct agents, Blitzy, n8n, and Refine. Clearly identify Direct agents as a category whose capabilities vary. Verify proposed competitor classifications against official sources before assigning symbols; check Refine claims against current code and documentation. Distinguish built-in support, integration/custom setup, varies, and undocumented support where applicable. Use a negative mark only for an explicitly established absence.

2. [ ] Task #2 - Build the visual comparison hierarchy.
   After Task #1, replace paragraph-heavy cells with symbols paired with brief visible labels and a small legend. Put Refine immediately after the capability column and emphasize it with the existing blue accent, stronger heading, and column background. Lead with three compact benefit callouts: use your agents and repositories; coordinate delivery across machines; keep ownership and recover work. Move longer qualifications and source explanations into native details/summary disclosures below the matrix. Preserve product links, source attribution, and an accurately maintained verification date. Include a concise link to the existing Get Started section.

3. [ ] Task #3 - Make the comparison usable across screen sizes.
   Implement scoped styles in src/surfaces/website/assets/site.css using the existing typography and palette. Keep the capability labels and Refine visible together at 320px and 390px widths; allow other columns to scroll within a labeled, keyboard-accessible region with a visible scroll cue. Use semantic table headers, adequate contrast, visible focus, and text alongside symbols so meaning does not depend on color. Supporting detail must work with keyboard and touch. Prefer HTML/CSS and native disclosures; this section does not require a new framework or generated imagery.

4. [ ] Task #4 - Update coverage and prepare the Quality handoff.
   Update tests/website_comparison_browser.test.js to reflect the new column order, shorter matrix, and disclosures instead of requiring eight prose rows. Preserve checks for product identity, sources, table semantics, and highlighting. Cover readable status labels, keyboard disclosure access, no page overflow, and initial Refine visibility at 1440, 1024, 390, and 320px. Quality should run node --test tests/website_comparison_browser.test.js with Playwright Chromium available, distinguish skipped tests from passes, and inspect desktop/mobile screenshots for scanability, clipping, and sticky-column overlap. The visual acceptance criterion is that visitors can identify the three reasons to choose Refine without opening supporting detail.

evidence: Inspected src/surfaces/website/index.html: #compare contains eight descriptive rows comparing Direct agents, Blitzy, n8n, and Refine, with existing sources.
Inspected src/surfaces/website/assets/site.css: the comparison uses a fixed-layout table with min-width: 1040px and Refine as the final column.

Inspected tests/website_comparison_browser.test.js and tests/support/web_app.js: existing browser coverage checks content, sources, keyboard scrolling, and four viewport widths; it skips when Playwright Chromium is unavailable.
default-plan.summary: Plan ready. The comparison currently gives equal weight to long descriptions, obscuring Refine’s advantages; its 1,040px minimum width also places Refine off-screen on phones. Replace that presentation with a compact visual capability matrix and prominent reasons to choose Refine, retaining supporting detail and sources. No files or workflow state changed.

default-plan.name: Plan
default-plan.prompt:
## Plan

Develop a plan to achieve the Goal's desired outcome. If the goal outcome is underspecified or is missing details add only just enough detail so that AI agents do not thrash or become confused.

### Outcome

A clear implementation plan that explains the approach and breaks the work into ordered tasks. Begin with a short description of the desired behavior and proposed solution. Use a numbered checklist, such as `Task #1 - What changes and why`. Include dependencies and important design decisions where they help implementation.

### Guardrails

- Read the context that helps explain the Goal and how the existing system works.
- Look for the underlying cause. Consider whether a missing or misused concept explains the problem, and improve that concept rather than adding fixes for individual symptoms.
- Give each task enough detail to guide implementation while leaving room for reasonable implementation choices.
- Keep the plan focused on the desired outcome. Prefer straightforward changes that fit the existing architecture.

{{templates.purpose}}

{{templates.architecture}}
